With POWER9
column2: each CPU thread has its own MMU context and can be

column1: in the host or a guest independently of the other threads; there is
still however a restriction that all threads must use the same type
of address translation
column2: either radix tree or hashed page table (HPT).

column1: Since we only support HPT guests on a HPT host at this point
can treat the threads as being independent
work of coordinating the CPU threads.  To make this simpler
introduce a new threads_per_vcore() function that returns 1 on
POWER9 and threads_per_subcore on POWER7/8
of threads_per_subcore or threads_per_core in various places.
This also changes the value of the KVM_CAP_PPC_SMT capability on
POWER9 systems from 4 to 1
column2: so that userspace will not try to

column1: create VMs with multiple vcpus per vcore.  (If userspace did create
a VM that thought it was in an SMT mode
column2: the VM might try to use

column1: the msgsndp instruction
column2: which will not work as expected.  In

column1: future it may be possible to trap and emulate msgsndp in order to
allow VMs to think they are in an SMT mode
of allowing migration from POWER8 systems.)
With all this
column2: we can now run guests on POWER9 as long as the host

column1: is running with HPT translation.  Since userspace currently has no
way to request radix tree translation for the guest
no choice but to use HPT translation.
